text:
Maya Chen: Heads up — multiple customers reporting JSON parse failures after last night's model rollout (redwood/gpt-instruct-2.2). Error rate for structured-output endpoints jumped to ~3.2% from ~0.05%. @Ravi can you pull the rollout logs? :rotating_light:

DeployBot: Deployed model redwood/gpt-instruct-2.2 to production (us-east-1) at 2026-03-16T23:40Z. Canary set to 25%.

Ravi Patel: Looking now. Any sample responses from customers?

AcmeApp_SRE: Here's one from our prod run — we call /v1/chat/complete with mode=json. Response fails our parser with "Invalid JSON: trailing comma". Snippet we received:
```json
{"user_id": "u-9832", "items": [{"sku":"x12","qty":1},],}
```
That trailing comma didn't appear in responses yesterday. We just started seeing it after the model change.

Julia Park: Got a repro locally. Re-run curl that customer used (model=redwood/gpt-instruct-2.2, system prompt requests strict schema). Example request:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/complete \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-instruct-2.2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You must output valid JSON exactly matching the schema"},{"role":"user","content":"Produce order JSON"}],"mode":"json"}'
```
And the output we get from 2.2: 
```json
{"user_id": 9832, "items": "[]", "metadata": null}
```
Notes: user_id is integer (should be string), items is a string not an array, and metadata key was added unexpectedly.

Maya Chen: That looks like schema drift — model seems to have changed generation style (types + extra keys). Any difference vs 2.1?

André Morgan: Confirmed on our canary logs — 2.1 returns strict JSON array/strings, 2.2 occasionally serializes arrays as strings and emits extra keys (metadata, debug). Rate of schema violations correlated with 2.2 traffic.

Ravi Patel: Opening incident INC-2026-142. Short-term options: rollback 2.2 rollout to 0% canary, add a validation layer to reject/clean bad JSON, or add a post-processing transformer that parses strings that look like JSON. Thoughts?

AcmeApp_SRE: Rollback would be appreciated. We can't tolerate parsing errors in prod — makes order processing fail. Also please advise on ETA for a fix and whether this triggers SLA credit.

Julia Park: Quick mitigation I tested: run a strict schema validator on the response and if it fails attempt JSON.parse on fields that are strings but look like arrays/objects (e.g., items=="[]" -> parse to []). It reduces customer-facing failures immediately. I'll push a short-lived middleware snippet to support for now.

Maya Chen: @DeployBot can you pause the rest of the rollout and revert canary to 0% for redwood/gpt-instruct-2.2?

DeployBot: Rollout paused. Reverting canary for redwood/gpt-instruct-2.2 to 0% in us-east-1.

Ravi Patel: Notes for engineering/ML: collect prompts that trigger the drift, save model outputs with token-level trace, and run comparison against 2.1 on same prompts. Need to determine whether this is a decoding/config change (temp settings) or a model behavior change introduced during fine-tune. Assigning to eng-ml.

André Morgan: I'll pull the kernel/runtime changes from the 2.2 rollout — also check any default temperature/formatting instruction changes. If it's config, we can fix without rollback of weight artifacts.

Maya Chen: Action items summary: 1) rollback canary -> done, 2) push validator middleware (Julia) -> in progress, 3) eng-ml investigation (Ravi/André) -> assigned, 4) respond to customer with mitigation + SLA path (Support) -> Julia to draft.

Julia Park: Draft reply to AcmeApp_SRE: "We've paused the 2.2 rollout and deployed a temporary validation/normalization middleware that will fix common type/stringification issues. We're investigating root cause and will update within 4 hours. If you experienced failures during the incident window we'll follow up on SLA credits." Will post to thread and send to customer.

AcmeApp_SRE: Thanks — appreciate the quick response. Will monitor for any further failures and share logs if I see new patterns. :thumbsup: 

Maya Chen: Adding a todo — add strict_schema flag to API so customers can opt-in to strict enforcement (reject bad JSON) vs best-effort normalization. That'll reduce ambiguity.

Support Bot: Incident INC-2026-142 created and linked to this thread. Priority: P1.

Ravi Patel: I'll update thread with investigation findings (repro corpus + diff) when ready. For now middleware + rollback should keep customers safe. :eyes:
